subject: Negative predictions in binomial model where missing observed data

messages.author: 329ee012aad3b9af
messages.subject: Negative predictions in binomial model where missing observed data
parts:
Hi all, I'm running a binomial model on survey data to obtain the probability(Y) among N observations.  

My problem:
Some predictions are negative values, which have no meaning as a probability (or as a count, for that matter).

My inla call:
formula <- Y ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym", graph=idn.adj) + 
f(age, model="rw2") + sex +
yrs_educ_agesex + 
logldipc_no_oilgas
result <- inla(formula, family="binomial", data=data, Ntrials=N,
quantile=c(0.025,0.5,0.975), 
control.family = list(link = "logit"), 
control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE), 
control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE, hyperpar=TRUE, mlik=TRUE))
predictions <- data.frame(NAME=data$ID_1, prov_num=data$prov_num, age=data$age, sex=data$sex, 
Y=data$Y, N=data$N, 
yrs_educ_agesex=data$yrs_educ_agesex, logldipc_no_oilgas=data$logldipc_no_oilgas,
pred = result$summary.fitted.values[,1], lower = result$summary.fitted.values[,3], 
upper = result$summary.fitted.values[,5])



About my data:
- The covariates have no missing values.  
- Y is missing (NA) for some rows.
- Predictions are only negative for rows where Y is missing.
- I have lots of observed zeroes for Y, and tiny sample sizes (<5) for N for some rows, but that should just affect the uncertainty intervals, not cause negative predictions.

What I have tried so far:
- Different N for the missing-Y rows (100, 0, NA).  Same negative values result.
- I thought maybe the predictions were still in logit-space instead of probabilities, but back-transforming them using exp(Ypred)/(1+exp(Ypred)) yielded nonsense results.

Am I missing something?  Attached is a subset of my data and predictions (pred, lower, upper).

messages.author: 329ee012aad3b9af
messages.subject: Re: Negative predictions in binomial model where missing observed data
parts:
Addendum:
There are also predicted values >1 for some rows where observed Y is missing, which is just as nonsensical as negative predictions.

I hope I'm just missing something simple . . . this is my first foray into INLA territory.  :)

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Negative predictions in binomial model where missing observed data
parts:
http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-How-can-I-do-predictions-using-INLA-

You need to tell inla to apply the link function to the missing observation predictors.
See link above, search for
  link=1

Finn
